entry.title: Evening — Nov 12, 2026
entry.content:
PulseBrief's Evening Pulse


Thu, Nov 12, 12:00 → Thu, Nov 12, 17:00


Cyber Security


Europol Dismantles Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC Infrastructure — 235 Servers, 257 Domains Seized


Nov 12, 15:07


Europol and partners from nine countries seized 235 servers and 257 domains used by the Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware operations as part of Operation Endgame. Authorities also recovered 6.4 million victim datasets from the criminal infrastructure. StealC had already been taken down once this year — German authorities traced the rebuilt network to the Virtualine bulletproof hosting provider, itself seized by the FBI in October.


Taking down three major malware-as-a-service operations simultaneously removes infrastructure supporting a significant portion of active ransomware and credential-theft campaigns — a direct reduction in threat actor capability.


Sources: BleepingComputer · The Record · Cybersecurity News


Windows SignDrop Zero-Day Grants SYSTEM Privileges — Public Exploit, No Patch


Nov 12, 16:04


Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri (Nightmare Eclipse) has released a public exploit for a new Windows zero-day that elevates standard user accounts to full SYSTEM privileges via the Common Log File System. Microsoft has not issued a CVE number or patch. The public availability of a working SYSTEM-level privilege escalation exploit means every Windows environment is immediately exposed with no vendor mitigation available.


An unpatched, publicly available Windows privilege escalation exploit is an active endpoint risk for every organization running Windows — threat actors will operationalize this rapidly.


Sources: BleepingComputer


ScreenConnect Campaign Update: CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9) Exploited — Not a New Zero-Day


Nov 12, 13:08


Blackpoint Cyber has clarified that the ongoing ScreenConnect campaign exploits a now-patched critical flaw, CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9), via a third-party plugin vulnerability — not a new zero-day as initially suggested. ConnectWise has disabled third-party extensions across roughly 400 partner environments. The auth bypass in the third-party tool could also allow MFA bypass, expanding the exposure model beyond credential compromise.


The clarification that a CVSS 9.9 flaw is being actively exploited via a third-party plugin changes remediation priorities for every MSP running ScreenConnect — extension audit is now critical.


Sources: The Hacker News · The Record · The Register


Citrix Patches CVSS 9.3 Authentication Bypass in NetScaler ADC and Gateway


Nov 12, 15:38


Citrix has released patches for 12 vulnerabilities across NetScaler ADC, NetScaler Gateway, and NetScaler Console, including CVE-2026-120868 (CVSS 9.3), a memory overflow enabling authentication bypass. Additional critical flaws in the same release could enable denial-of-service. NetScaler products are widely deployed as enterprise network access controllers and remote access gateways, making authentication bypass particularly high-impact.


An authentication bypass in a widely deployed enterprise gateway product is an immediate exploitation target — patching should be treated as urgent for any organization running NetScaler.


Sources: The Hacker News


CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Outlook Zero-Day CVE-2026-124194 — NTLMv2 Hash Leakage


Nov 12, 14:11


CISA has added CVE-2026-124194 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, confirming in-the-wild exploitation of the Microsoft Outlook flaw that leaks NTLMv2 credential hashes when a victim opens a specially crafted message. The November Patch Tuesday update containing the fix is still failing to install on some systems due to KB5132061 errors. Organizations where the patch fails to apply remain actively exposed with no Microsoft-provided workaround.


An actively exploited credential-theft flaw in Outlook with a broken patch rollout is an unresolved live risk — IT teams need to identify systems where KB5132061 failed and implement compensating controls.


Sources: Cybersecurity News · The Register


Qilin Ransomware Admin Identified as Russian National Aleksey Yakovtsev


Nov 12, 13:42


KrebsOnSecurity has linked Qilin ransomware's administrator to Aleksey Mikhailovich Yakovtsev, a 36-year-old residing in St. Petersburg, Russia, connecting the online identity 'Haise' to forum accounts, Telegram records, and leaked databases. Qilin has been responsible for attacks on hospitals, critical infrastructure, and major enterprises globally. The identification is a research finding rather than a formal legal charge, but represents significant attribution progress on one of the more active ransomware operations.


Attribution of a major ransomware administrator provides threat intelligence context for defenders and signals which jurisdictions have operational exposure — relevant for anyone tracking Qilin as a threat actor.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Red Hat Quay Critical Flaw (CVSS 9.8) Allows Unauthenticated Registry Takeover and Image Theft


Nov 12, 13:57


A critical vulnerability in Red Hat Quay, CVE-2026-123710 (CVSS 9.8), allows an unauthenticated attacker to take over a registry's token signing and read or overwrite all private container images. With anonymous access enabled by default, no account is required; with it disabled, any valid account suffices. Red Hat has released fixed builds.


Private container registries hold production application artifacts — unauthenticated takeover is a direct software supply chain risk for any organization running Red Hat Quay.


Sources: The Hacker News · Cybersecurity News


186 Fake AI Domains Serving ClickFix Lures and Search-Hijacking Browser Malware


Nov 12, 15:15


Researchers at Island have identified 186 lookalike domains impersonating popular AI tools — ChatGPT, Claude, Midjourney, and others — that redirect users to ClickFix-style clipboard injection lures, browser-hijacking extensions, and search redirectors. The campaign, codenamed TypoPrompting, exploits users' muscle memory for navigating to AI tools. The scale and variety of delivery mechanisms suggest an organized, sustained operation.


AI brand impersonation as a malware delivery vector is now a mature campaign category — any organization where employees regularly access AI tools needs browser security controls and user awareness training.


Sources: The Hacker News


AI & Machine Learning


Colette Kress Takes Nvidia Helm as Interim CEO — Next Earnings Call Now Most Consequential in Company History


Nov 12, 14:14


Nvidia CFO Colette Kress has assumed the interim CEO role following Jensen Huang's resignation. Kress helped architect Nvidia's financial transformation into a $3 trillion company and has deep relationships with hyperscaler customers, but has never led product strategy or served as a public technology visionary in the way Huang did. Nvidia's earnings call next week — which will now feature Kress in the CEO seat — is being described as the most important in the company's history given the leadership vacuum and national security backdrop.


Nvidia's interim CEO will set the tone for how the world's AI infrastructure crown jewel navigates a simultaneous governance crisis, congressional investigation, and earnings disclosure — the outcome shapes AI infrastructure confidence industry-wide.


Sources: Wired · TechCrunch


AI Chatbots Recommending Fake Retail Websites — ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity All Implicated


Nov 12, 17:00


A study by IP protection firm Podqi tested ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity with shopping queries across 151 brands and found all three directed users to imposter and risky websites when asked where to buy products or find regional storefronts. The hallucination problem extends beyond factual inaccuracies into active consumer fraud facilitation. The findings arrive just before the holiday shopping season when AI-assisted product research peaks.


AI-generated shopping recommendations directing consumers to fraud sites is a reputational and liability risk for any retailer whose brand is being impersonated — and a direct consumer trust problem for AI platform providers.


Sources: The Verge


United Airlines Formally Bans AI Agents From Booking Flights


Nov 12, 15:37


United Airlines has prohibited AI agents from logging into customer accounts to make bookings, citing privacy risks, unintended purchase liability, and federal regulations requiring passengers to personally attest their baggage doesn't contain hazardous materials. AI agents can still surface flight information but cannot transact. The policy is preemptive — United says agent booking volume is currently low but expects it to grow rapidly.


A major regulated-industry operator drawing a formal line against AI agent transactions sets a precedent that will propagate to aviation, financial services, and healthcare — a direct signal for anyone building or deploying transactional AI agents.


Sources: The Register


AWS MCP Gateway SSRF Flaw Allowed Authenticated Attackers to Reach Internal Networks and Cloud Credentials


Nov 12, 13:51


AWS has patched CVE-2026-125926, a server-side request forgery vulnerability in its open-source mcp-gateway-registry affecting versions 1.0.3 through 1.34.0. An authenticated attacker could exploit the flaw to route requests through the gateway to internal services and harvest cloud credentials. Version 1.35.0 contains the fix. The vulnerability is particularly significant given MCP gateways often run with elevated cloud permissions to serve AI agents.


An SSRF in the AWS MCP Gateway is a direct cloud credential theft vector for any organization running AI agent tooling on AWS infrastructure — upgrade to 1.35.0 immediately.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Norwest Closes $4B Fund With Deeper AI Focus — Largest in Firm's History


Nov 12, 15:18


Norwest Venture Partners has closed a $4 billion fund, its largest ever, with an explicit push deeper into AI investments across enterprise software, infrastructure, and applied AI. The fund size reflects continued LP appetite for AI exposure despite broader venture market caution. Norwest has existing positions across the AI stack from infrastructure to applications.


A $4B AI-focused fund from a major multi-stage firm signals sustained institutional capital commitment to AI investment — a market conditions indicator for founders and competing investors.


Sources: TechCrunch


Technology


Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 Enter 'Permanently Vulnerable' Era as Support Ends


Nov 12, 14:55


Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 have reached end of support, meaning they will no longer receive security updates — entering what The Register calls their 'permanently vulnerable' era. Organizations still running these versions face an expanding unpatched attack surface with no Microsoft-provided remediation path. Exchange has historically been a primary target for nation-state and ransomware actors.


Exchange servers at end of support with no patch path are an immediate upgrade priority — any organization still running 2016 or 2019 is now operating an increasingly indefensible mail infrastructure.


Sources: The Register


IBM Plans to Scale Beyond 1,000 Qubits in 2027 With Nighthawk r3 Processor


Nov 12, 13:37


IBM has announced plans to release the Nighthawk r3 quantum processor in 2027, which will exceed 1,000 qubits and serve as a component in future fault-tolerant quantum computing systems. The roadmap represents a significant milestone in IBM's quantum scaling trajectory. Fault-tolerant quantum computing at this scale begins to threaten current cryptographic assumptions that underpin most enterprise and government security infrastructure.


IBM's 1,000+ qubit roadmap for 2027 is a concrete post-quantum cryptography planning signal — any organization not yet assessing PQC migration timelines needs to start now.


Sources: The Register


Google Cloud Warns AMD Turin CPU Side-Channel Flaws Can Leak Data Across Processes in VMs


Nov 12, 12:09


Google Cloud has disclosed three side-channel vulnerabilities in AMD Turin (EPYC 9th gen) CPUs that allow an attacker with code on the same processor core to infer data from other processes or the kernel within a VM. Google has already applied between-VM mitigations; guest OS patches and a stop-and-start cycle are required to fully remediate within-VM exposure. AMD Turin is one of the newest server CPU generations deployed across cloud infrastructure.


CPU side-channel flaws in cloud VMs require tenant-side action — any organization running workloads on AMD Turin-based Google Cloud instances needs to apply guest OS patches and restart affected instances.


Sources: The Hacker News


Nintendo Executes Massive GitHub DMCA Sweep — Switch Emulators and Mod Chip Firmware Taken Down


Nov 12, 16:29


Nintendo has filed a large wave of DMCA takedowns on GitHub targeting Switch emulators and mod chip firmware repositories, with IGN reporting the sweep is significantly broader than previous enforcement actions. The move comes as Nintendo prepares for its next console launch and signals an aggressive IP enforcement posture. The Hacker News discussion has accumulated 223 points, reflecting significant developer and gaming community concern about software preservation.


A major DMCA sweep targeting emulators and firmware sets enforcement precedents that affect software preservation, security research, and the broader emulation ecosystem.


Sources: IGN via Hacker News


Microsoft Teams Outage Hits North America Users


Nov 12, 16:44


Microsoft is investigating a Teams outage affecting users across North America, tracked under TM1550488 in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Automated recovery measures are reducing the disruption but service has not fully restored. The outage arrives in the same week as the broken November Patch Tuesday update and SQL Server performance issues, compounding Microsoft platform reliability concerns.


A Teams outage affecting North American users during business hours is an immediate operational disruption for any Microsoft 365-dependent organization — monitor the admin center for restoration status.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Lenovo ThinkSystem V4 Firmware Flaw Restores Default Root Credentials After Factory Reset


Nov 12, 13:37


Lenovo has disclosed CVE-2026-81936, a high-severity flaw in ThinkSystem V4 server management firmware where a factory reset restores a default OpenBMC root password rather than generating a new one. An attacker who knows the default credential can access administrative interfaces and the controller's underlying OS after any reset. The flaw affects server management firmware, which runs continuously regardless of host OS state.


A BMC-level credential restoration flaw on a major server platform survives OS reinstallation — any organization running ThinkSystem V4 servers needs to patch firmware and audit BMC access controls.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Business & Markets


Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO — CFO Colette Kress Named Interim


Nov 12, 13:58


Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO on Thursday after the company opened an internal investigation into his affair with Alice Huang, identified by US intelligence as a Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. Huang has since agreed to testify before Congress, where he faces questions about the national security implications of the relationship. The leadership vacuum at the world's dominant AI chip company — with earnings next week — represents the most consequential corporate event in the technology sector.


The removal of Nvidia's founder-CEO reshapes AI infrastructure supply chains, US-China chip competition, and the AI investment landscape simultaneously — nothing else touches more of what matters right now.


Sources: Wired · TechCrunch · The Register · NYT · TechCrunch (Congress)


Trump Floats Tim Cook as Jensen Huang's Nvidia Successor


Nov 12, 16:12


President Trump posted on Truth Social suggesting Apple chairman Tim Cook should take over as Nvidia CEO following Jensen Huang's resignation. The post signals the White House intends to influence the successor selection at a company controlling the dominant AI chip supply. It also underscores the degree to which Nvidia's leadership transition is being treated as a matter of national interest rather than a purely corporate decision.


Presidential intervention in a private company's CEO succession is extraordinary — it signals that Nvidia's leadership is now a geopolitical matter, not just a governance one.


Sources: TechCrunch


Five Ways Jensen Huang's Ouster Could Damage the AI Industry


Nov 12, 16:32


TechCrunch analysis identifies specific structural risks from Huang's departure: his personal relationships with hyperscaler CEOs, his role as the industry's de facto infrastructure evangelist, and Nvidia's pipeline decisions that were driven by his vision rather than committee consensus. Beyond governance, Huang was actively steering compute allocation and pricing in ways that benefited the broader ecosystem. His absence creates decision-making vacuums across the AI supply chain simultaneously.


Understanding the second-order effects of Huang's departure is essential for anyone dependent on Nvidia GPU roadmaps, pricing, or supply allocation decisions.


Sources: TechCrunch


Daylight Raises $80M for AI-Powered Security Operations


Nov 12, 13:12


Daylight has closed an $80 million funding round to accelerate its AI-powered security operations platform, with plans to expand US presence and enter new markets. The raise reflects continued investor conviction in AI-native SOC tooling as organizations seek to match AI-assisted attack speeds with AI-assisted defense. Daylight competes in an increasingly crowded AI security operations category alongside established players and well-funded startups.


An $80M raise in AI-powered SOC tooling signals where enterprise security budget is flowing — a vendor landscape signal for anyone evaluating or procuring security operations platforms.


Sources: SecurityWeek


Austria Passes New Espionage Law Targeting Russian Intelligence Operations


Nov 12, 16:26


Austria has enacted new legislation specifically targeting Russian espionage, closing what Foreign Minister Beate Meinl-Reisinger described as a historic 'blind spot' in Austrian counterintelligence law. Austria has long been criticized as a permissive environment for foreign intelligence operations due to its neutrality status and Vienna's role as an international hub. The law represents a significant shift in Austrian security posture amid the broader European response to Russian hybrid operations.


A new Austrian espionage law targeting Russia changes the operating environment for intelligence activities across one of Europe's most historically permissive jurisdictions — a signal for any organization with Vienna-based operations or sensitive European personnel.


Sources: Politico EU


Data Centers Will Continue to Be Built Despite Voter Pushback — Tech Giants Have Resources to Weather Delays


Nov 12, 14:42


The New York Times reports that despite midterm election results reflecting voter opposition to AI data center construction — driven by energy and water consumption concerns — major technology companies have the financial and political resources to weather delays and continue buildout. Hyperscalers are pursuing alternative sites, private power arrangements, and regulatory workarounds to maintain expansion timelines. The piece contextualizes the voter backlash as a friction factor rather than a fundamental constraint.


Understanding which AI infrastructure buildout constraints are real versus political noise is essential for anyone planning compute procurement or data center investment timelines.


Sources: New York Times

entry.title: Afternoon — Nov 12, 2026
entry.content:
PulseBrief's Afternoon Pulse


Thu, Nov 12, 06:00 → Thu, Nov 12, 12:00


Cyber Security


4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts Used to Plant CI Secret Stealer Across 1,800+ Repositories


Nov 12, 06:42


An attacker used stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts to inject a secret-stealing payload into repositories those accounts had write access to, running malicious CI workflows in at least 1,806 repositories. The stealer is designed to harvest secrets and cloud credentials that CI pipelines can reach — tokens, API keys, and cloud provider credentials. The attack is a live, large-scale GitHub supply chain compromise affecting any organization whose repositories were accessible to compromised accounts.


A coordinated CI credential-theft campaign hitting nearly 2,000 repositories is an active supply chain threat — any team with open-source contributors or shared GitHub org access needs to audit recent workflow runs and rotate secrets immediately.


Sources: The Hacker News


New N-central Exploits Bypass Hotfix 2 — Root RCE and Windows SYSTEM Access Still Possible


Nov 12, 09:39


Researchers disclosed additional N-central vulnerabilities that work against servers running the just-released Hotfix 2, with exploits enabling root-level remote code execution and Windows SYSTEM access. N-able says the new server-side issue requires a non-default configuration with the Legacy API exposed to the internet, but the client-side exploit has no such prerequisite. Active exploitation began almost immediately after the original 33 zero-days dropped, and the patch cycle is still incomplete.


An RMM platform where the patch doesn't fully close the door is a live supply chain risk — MSPs running N-central need to verify Legacy API exposure and treat downstream customer environments as potentially compromised.


Sources: The Hacker News · SecurityWeek


Google Session Hijacking Campaign Active Since August — Live Proxy Bypasses All Standard Link Defenses


Nov 12, 11:51


A phishing operation dubbed Operation CloudFire has been stealing live Google sessions from corporate users since mid-August 2026 using calendar invites and real-time reverse proxies that make attacker links appear legitimate to every standard detection check. Material Security's threat research team has taken down hundreds of attacker domains, but the campaign continues. The live-proxy technique captures session tokens in real time, bypassing MFA and making stolen sessions immediately usable.


A campaign that defeats standard phishing link detection and bypasses MFA by stealing live sessions is an active threat to any organization running Google Workspace — detection must shift to session anomaly monitoring, not link scanning.


Sources: The Hacker News


Notion Customer Data Exposed in Fireworks AI Breach — Chat Transcripts Accessed Across Workspaces


Nov 12, 11:08


Attackers who breached AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI accessed chat transcripts for fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces, with Notion confirming the compromise stems from a third-party vendor incident rather than a direct breach of its own systems. Most transcripts could not be attributed to specific users. The incident is another example of AI platform vendors becoming a data exposure vector for their enterprise customers.


A breach at an AI vendor exposing enterprise workspace chat data is a third-party risk signal for any organization using AI-powered features built on shared infrastructure — vendor AI supply chains need the same scrutiny as traditional SaaS.


Sources: SecurityWeek


PTC Patches CVSS 9.2 RCE Flaw in Windchill and FlexPLM — Deserialization Bug Requires No Authentication


Nov 12, 11:33


PTC has patched CVE-2026-126325, a critical improper input validation and deserialization flaw in its Windchill PLM and FlexPLM platforms scoring 9.2 on CVSSv4, which could allow remote code execution without authentication. Windchill is widely deployed in manufacturing, aerospace, and defense supply chains for product lifecycle management. No active exploitation has been confirmed, but the CVSS score and attack complexity make this a high-priority patch.


A near-perfect CVSS score RCE in a PLM platform used across manufacturing and defense supply chains is an immediate patching priority for any organization running Windchill or FlexPLM.


Sources: The Hacker News


GSocket Abused by Multiple Threat Actors for Persistent Linux Server Access After Patching


Nov 12, 09:38


Multiple threat actor groups are deploying GSocket, a legitimate open-source tool that tunnels traffic through Google's infrastructure, to maintain persistent backdoor access to compromised Linux servers even after the initial vulnerability is patched. Because GSocket is a legitimate tool and uses Google's network, it blends with normal traffic and evades many detection controls. The multi-actor adoption suggests GSocket has become an established persistence technique in the threat actor community.


A persistence technique that survives patching and hides inside legitimate Google infrastructure traffic is a detection gap for any organization running Linux servers — threat hunting should include GSocket process and network indicators.


Sources: BleepingComputer


AI-Generated Scripts Enabled Lateral Movement in Minutes During US Retailer Breach


Nov 12, 11:00


Dark Reading details a breach of a US retailer where the attacker initially failed using hand-typed commands, then pivoted to AI-generated attack scripts that achieved lateral movement within minutes. The case study illustrates how AI is lowering the skill floor for post-exploitation activity, compressing the attacker's time-to-pivot dramatically. The retailer's defenses were calibrated for human-speed attack progression and were not designed to detect AI-accelerated lateral movement.


AI-assisted lateral movement that defeats defenses tuned for human attack speeds is a direct signal to revisit detection logic and response time assumptions for any organization with a retail or e-commerce attack surface.


Sources: Dark Reading


Microsoft Confirms November Patch Tuesday Update Failing to Install — Exploited Outlook Flaw Remains Unpatched on Affected Systems


Nov 12, 10:24


Microsoft has officially confirmed that KB5132061 fails to install on Windows 11 systems that received the October preview update, throwing error codes 0x80070306, 0x800f0989, and 0x800f0993. The broken update includes the patch for an actively exploited Outlook vulnerability that leaks NTLMv2 credential hashes. Microsoft has not yet issued a workaround, leaving affected systems exposed to an in-the-wild credential-theft exploit with no available remediation.


Systems that cannot install the update remain actively exposed to an exploited NTLMv2 hash-leaking Outlook flaw — IT teams need to identify affected systems and monitor for workaround guidance from Microsoft.


Sources: BleepingComputer


AI & Machine Learning


Anthropic IPO Goes Live — S-1 Portal Active, 641 HN Points Signal Intense Market Interest


Nov 12, 11:46


Anthropic's IPO registration portal is now publicly accessible, with Hacker News discussion accumulating 641 points and 650 comments — among the highest engagement of any recent tech IPO. The listing follows reporting that set the price range at $70–$78/share implying a valuation approaching $1.4 trillion, and analysis raising governance concerns about investor-partner overlaps with Amazon and Google. The IPO represents the first public market test for a frontier AI safety lab.


Anthropic going public is the defining AI market event of 2026 — the valuation, governance structure, and investor reception will set pricing and governance benchmarks for the entire frontier AI sector.


Sources: Anthropic IPO Portal · Hacker News


ScreenConnect Campaign Update: Vulnerability in Legitimate Extension Bypassed Authentication — Not Credential Compromise


Nov 12, 10:39


SecurityWeek reports that the active ScreenConnect campaign exploited a vulnerability in a legitimate third-party extension to bypass authentication, clarifying earlier reporting that had pointed to compromised partner credentials. The distinction matters: an exploitable extension vulnerability means any ScreenConnect deployment running the affected extension was potentially reachable, not just those with weak credentials. ConnectWise has disabled five third-party extensions across partner environments.


An authentication bypass via a legitimate extension changes the exposure model for the ScreenConnect campaign — MSPs need to audit which extensions are installed, not just review credential hygiene.


Sources: SecurityWeek


Nvidia Board Weighing Jensen Huang's Future as Second Affair Report Surfaces


Nov 12, 07:03


Nvidia's board is actively evaluating Jensen Huang's position following reports of a second alleged affair — this one with Nvidia VP of Healthcare Kimberly Powell, a direct report — compounding the earlier admitted relationship with Alice Huang, identified by US intelligence as a Chinese spy. Nvidia stock dropped more than 8% in after-hours trading. The board's decision, expected imminently, will determine leadership continuity at the company controlling the dominant AI chip supply.


The potential removal of Nvidia's founder-CEO is the most consequential corporate event in AI infrastructure right now — any organization dependent on Nvidia GPU supply or pricing needs to monitor this closely.


Sources: Euronews Business


European Tech Buyers Adding Digital Sovereignty to Security Procurement — EU-Headquartered Vendor Sales Surge


Nov 12, 11:31


A Register analysis finds European enterprise technology buyers are now explicitly adding digital sovereignty requirements to security procurement decisions, driving a significant increase in sales for EU-headquartered vendors over the past two years. The trend is attributed to a combination of the Trump administration's posture toward European allies, and mandatory compliance with NIS2 and DORA regulations that heighten scrutiny of non-EU vendor data handling. US vendors are increasingly being asked to demonstrate data residency and access controls that meet EU sovereignty standards.


Digital sovereignty is shifting from a compliance checkbox to an active procurement filter in European markets — a direct signal for any vendor selling into Europe or any organization building a European vendor strategy.


Sources: The Register


Node.js Patches Unauthenticated HTTP/2 Server Crash and Cross-Connection Memory Leak


Nov 12, 08:20


Node.js released fixes for 16 vulnerabilities including two critical HTTP/2 flaws: one allowing unauthenticated clients to crash servers on the 24.x and 26.x lines, and a second that causes servers to send memory contents — including other clients' response data — to requesting clients. Fixed versions are 22.23.5, 24.22.3, and 26.13.1. HTTP/2 is enabled by default in many Node.js server configurations, making the crash and data-leak flaws broadly applicable.


An unauthenticated server crash combined with a cross-connection memory leak in Node.js HTTP/2 is an immediate patching priority for any organization running Node.js web services or APIs.


Sources: The Hacker News


Technology


Critical Red Hat Quay Flaw Could Expose Private Container Images and Allow Repository Takeover


Nov 12, 09:23


A critical vulnerability in Red Hat Quay, the enterprise container registry, could allow attackers to access private container images, overwrite repositories, and establish persistent access to the registry. The flaw affects organizations running Quay as their internal container image store, which often contains production application code and configuration. Red Hat has released a patch.


Private container registries hold production application artifacts — a flaw enabling image theft and repository overwrite is a direct software supply chain risk for any organization using Red Hat Quay.


Sources: SecurityWeek


Pre-Auth MongoDB Crash Flaw (CVE-2026-118383) Triggers on Failover — Replica Set Members at Risk


Nov 12, 09:25


A critical unauthenticated vulnerability in MongoDB Server allows an attacker to send two crafted requests that crash a replica set member; the crash is triggered specifically when that member is elected as primary during a failover, creating a targeted availability attack. MongoDB has released fixed versions. The exploit path — crashing a server that then becomes primary — could be used to repeatedly destabilize replica sets during high-availability failover events.


A pre-auth crash exploit that activates on MongoDB failover is a targeted availability threat for any production database cluster — patch immediately and review replica set monitoring for anomalous failover patterns.


Sources: The Hacker News


Rockstar Games UK Workers Vote on Union Recognition Ahead of GTA VI Launch


Nov 12, 11:01


UK staff at Rockstar Games are voting on formal union recognition, with the outcome expected before the high-stakes GTA VI launch. A separate union-busting dispute is proceeding toward resolution concurrently. The vote at one of the world's most commercially significant game studios — GTA VI is expected to be the highest-grossing entertainment launch in history — adds labor relations risk to an already complex release window.


Labor action at Rockstar ahead of GTA VI is a material risk signal for the gaming industry's largest anticipated release — a signal for anyone tracking games sector workforce dynamics or entertainment supply chain risk.


Sources: The Register


Business & Markets


Spirit Airlines Flight Attendants Union Negotiated Data Scrubbing From $10M Google Data Sale


Nov 12, 10:15


The union representing Spirit Airlines flight attendants successfully negotiated with Google to have sensitive employee records removed from a $10 million data sale before the transaction closed, after learning Google had sought access to Spirit's data assets during the airline's bankruptcy proceedings. The case illustrates how labor organizations can intervene in corporate data transactions to protect member privacy — a tactic likely to be replicated as AI training data demand drives acquisitions of bankrupt companies' data estates.


A union successfully blocking employee data from an AI training data sale sets a precedent for workforce data rights in corporate distress scenarios — a signal for HR, legal, and privacy teams at any organization with unionized staff.


Sources: Wired


EU Court Rejects Poland's Challenge to Seven Major Climate Laws — Green Transition Legal Framework Upheld


Nov 12, 11:25


The European Court of Justice has dismissed Poland's legal challenges to seven significant EU climate laws, cases originally launched by the previous nationalist government and kept alive under the current pro-EU administration. The ruling reinforces the legal durability of the EU's green transition regulatory framework against member state resistance. Organizations operating in the EU can now plan against these climate laws with greater certainty that they will not be overturned through legal challenge.


Court confirmation that seven EU climate laws are legally sound removes a key uncertainty for any organization with EU sustainability compliance obligations or clean energy investment in Europe.


Sources: Politico EU

entry.title: Morning — Nov 12, 2026
entry.content:
PulseBrief's Morning Pulse


Wed, Nov 11, 17:00 → Thu, Nov 12, 06:00


Cyber Security


ScreenConnect Campaign Breaches 48 MSPs, Deploys Rogue Remote-Access Clients to 288+ Endpoints


Nov 11, 24:00


An active malware campaign is exploiting compromised ScreenConnect environments to push rogue remote-access clients across MSP customer networks, with ConnectWise confirming at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations affected. ConnectWise has disabled five third-party extensions in partner environments as a precaution and says there is no evidence of a core ScreenConnect vulnerability — suggesting compromised partner credentials or extensions as the entry point. The attack pattern mirrors the supply chain risk model: compromise the management tool, reach all downstream customers.


An active campaign systematically using MSP remote access infrastructure to compromise dozens of organizations is a live supply chain threat affecting any business managed by an affected MSP.


Sources: BleepingComputer · The Hacker News


Critical Apache HTTP/2 RCE Vulnerability — CVE-2026-119618 — Affects Versions 2.4.55 Through 2.4.70


Nov 12, 24:00


A critical remote code execution vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 module has been patched in version 2.4.71, released yesterday. CVE-2026-119618 allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute code on affected servers running HTTP/2 — which is enabled by default in many configurations. Apache HTTP Server is one of the most widely deployed web servers globally, and the Hacker News discussion has topped 1,100 points, indicating significant community concern.


An unauthenticated RCE in the world's most deployed web server is an immediate patching priority for any organization running Apache 2.4.55–2.4.70 with HTTP/2 enabled.


Sources: The Hacker News · Wiz


Chinese AI System Scrapes Open-Source Data to Identify and Target Spies in Taiwan's Chip Industry


Nov 12, 24:00


Dark Reading reports that the Chinese Communist Party has built a Big Data AI system that scrapes publicly available information to identify, profile, and potentially recruit or exploit individuals working in Taiwan's semiconductor industry. The system is described as a scalable, automated version of the Alice Huang playbook — systematically finding and targeting people with access to sensitive chip technology. The disclosure comes as the Nvidia/Megaspeed affair has put China's semiconductor intelligence operations under intense scrutiny.


An AI system purpose-built to identify espionage targets in the chip industry is a direct threat intelligence signal for anyone working in semiconductor R&D, chip supply chains, or AI hardware — especially those with China exposure.


Sources: Dark Reading


Baker Tilly Notifies Clients of Third-Party Data Breach Exposing Personal Information


Nov 11, 24:00


Baker Tilly Advisory Group, one of the largest US accounting and advisory firms, is notifying clients that a breach at a third-party provider compromised personal information about clients and their dependents. The specifics of what data was exposed and which third-party vendor was breached have not been fully disclosed. A breach at a top-10 US accounting firm touching client personal data is a direct risk signal for any organization that uses Baker Tilly for audit, tax, or advisory services.


Sources: BleepingComputer


AI & Machine Learning


Google Launches Gemini Decisions API — Structured Decision-Making Layer for AI Agents


Nov 11, 24:00


Google has released the Gemini Decisions API, a new interface designed to give AI agents a structured way to make and explain decisions across multi-step workflows. The API surfaces decision logic in a form that developers and auditors can inspect, addressing a key enterprise objection to agentic AI: opacity about why an agent took a particular action. The Hacker News thread has nearly 500 points, indicating strong developer interest.


A structured, inspectable decision layer for Gemini agents directly addresses enterprise AI governance requirements — a capability signal for any team building or evaluating agentic AI systems.


Sources: Google Blog


United Airlines Bans AI Agents From Booking Flights — Privacy and Regulatory Compliance Cited


Nov 11, 24:00


United Airlines has formally prohibited personal AI agents from logging into customer accounts and making flight bookings on their behalf, citing customer privacy risks, the potential for unintended purchases, and federal regulatory requirements — including rules requiring customers to personally attest their baggage doesn't contain hazardous materials. AI agents can still surface United flight information but cannot transact. United says it has not yet seen significant volume of agent booking attempts, but is acting preemptively.


A major airline drawing a formal line against AI agent transactions sets a precedent for how regulated industries will handle AI agent authorization — a direct signal for anyone building or deploying AI agents in consumer-facing or compliance-sensitive workflows.


Sources: New York Times · CBS News · The Verge


OpenAI Commits $2M to Children's AI Safety Research — Funds Shared Risk Measurement Tools


Nov 12, 24:00


OpenAI has announced a $2 million commitment to fund research on AI's impact on children's safety, including development of shared tools for measuring both risks and opportunities for young users. The announcement comes in the same news cycle as Wired's report on a teenager who used Google Gemini on a school Chromebook to plan her suicide for months without being flagged. Huawei Open-Sources MACaQ — Internal Model Quantizer for Local Inference Without Cloud Dependency


Nov 11, 24:00


Huawei has released MACaQ, its internal model quantization toolkit designed for efficient local inference, as open source on GitHub. The tool enables organizations to run quantized AI models on local hardware without sending data to cloud providers — a capability with significant privacy and sovereignty implications. The release comes as China continues to push domestic AI infrastructure independence and signals Huawei's intent to influence the open-source AI tooling ecosystem.

Sources: GitHub


Voter Backlash Against AI Could Threaten Data Center Buildout — Economists See Potential Upside


Nov 11, 24:00


A New York Times analysis explores how growing voter opposition to AI data centers — driven by energy consumption, water use, and local land-use concerns — is translating into political pressure that could slow or block new construction. Some economists argue this friction could actually redirect AI investment toward more productive uses rather than raw infrastructure accumulation. AWS Launches Local Cloud Emulator That Runs on a PC — Full API Compatibility for Offline Development

Amazon Web Services has released an AWS emulator that runs locally on a developer's PC, providing API-compatible access to cloud services without an internet connection. The tool enables developers to build, test, and iterate against AWS APIs in fully offline or air-gapped environments, eliminating cloud costs and latency during development. US Data Center Energy Demand Growing 10x Faster Than Grid Capacity — Operators Racing to Self-Supply Power


Nov 11, 24:00


A new analysis finds that US data center electricity demand is expanding ten times faster than the grid's ability to add new capacity, forcing hyperscalers and colocation operators to pursue private power generation, longer interconnection queues, and in some cases on-site natural gas or nuclear arrangements. The mismatch is already causing years-long delays in bringing new data center capacity online in power-constrained markets like Northern Virginia, Phoenix, and the Chicago suburbs.

Sources: The Register


Yandex Reports Drone Attacks on Its Datacenters Caused Data Loss — Now Enabling Backups by Default


Nov 12, 24:00


Russian cloud provider Yandex has disclosed that drone attacks on its data center infrastructure caused data loss for some customers, marking a rare public acknowledgment of physical infrastructure destruction impacting cloud services. In response, Yandex is enabling backup replication by default for all customers and has hinted that some on-premises infrastructure resilience is warranted. The incident is the first publicly confirmed case of drone warfare directly causing cloud data loss.

Sources: The Register


EU Proposes Digital Fairness Act — Targeting Loot Boxes, Addictive Design, and Undisclosed Influencer Marketing


Nov 11, 24:00


The European Commission has published the proposed Digital Fairness Act, targeting online practices that exploit consumers including gaming loot boxes, addictive design features in social media and apps, misleading pricing, and undisclosed influencer advertising. The regulation would apply to gaming, e-commerce, and social media platforms operating in the EU market. The DFA extends the EU's digital regulatory framework beyond large platform obligations (DSA/DMA) into broader consumer protection for all online services.

Nov 11, 24:00

Nov 11, 24:00


House Republicans have issued a deadline for Jensen Huang to agree to a closed-door national security briefing on his relationship with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang. Nov 11, 24:00


UK-based Fractile has closed a $720 million funding round, making it one of the top-funded companies in the race to build purpose-built AI inference chips as alternatives to Nvidia GPUs. SoftBank and Nvidia Lead $8.5B Round for German Robotics Startup Agile Robots


Nov 12, 24:00


Agile Robots, a German humanoid and industrial robotics startup, has raised a major round at an $8.5 billion valuation led by SoftBank, with Nvidia also participating. The company plans to expand US operations and scale European production. The investment signals continued aggressive capital deployment into physical AI — robots that can operate in unstructured environments — following similar large rounds for Figure, 1X, and Physical Intelligence.

Sources: New York Times

Nov 11, 24:00


CoreWeave's Q3 earnings reveal the GPU cloud provider is increasingly requiring customers to pay upfront, borrowing against specific contracts, and moving toward shorter-term deals that carry higher pricing. The strategy reflects the capital intensity of building out GPU clusters to meet AI demand while managing cash flow without traditional financing runway. The shift to shorter contracts with premium pricing signals CoreWeave is prioritizing financial flexibility over long-term lock-in.

Japan is deploying emergency cybersecurity funding that will add public-private cyber response capacity, establish an AI-focused security team under the economic ministry, and expand the government's authority to use its newly enacted active cyber-defense powers. The package responds to a documented rise in AI-assisted intrusions targeting Japanese government and critical infrastructure. Japan's active cyber-defense law, passed earlier this year, allows offensive countermeasures — expanding the new team's potential mandate.

Poland has taken its ePUAP platform offline after a cyberattack, disrupting a nationwide system that handles official document submissions, communication with government agencies, and administrative procedures for millions of citizens. Iran-Backed Network Directed Physical Attacks on London Synagogues and US Bank Buildings via FaceTime


Nov 11, 16:57


A US indictment unsealed Tuesday details how an Iran-backed network directed physical attacks on Jewish and American targets across Europe — including synagogues in Belgium, the Netherlands, and London, and US bank buildings in Amsterdam and Paris — over FaceTime. The revelations connect Iranian state direction to real-world violence against Western targets, expanding beyond the cyber and hybrid sabotage operations attributed to Iran in recent weeks.


Iranian state-directed physical attacks on Western targets coordinated via consumer apps represent a significant escalation of hybrid operations — a threat intelligence signal for any organization or institution with a potential Iran threat nexus.


Sources: The Record


N-able Releases Emergency N-central Hotfix After 33 Zero-Days Forced Global Shutdown

N-able has released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 addressing seven published CVEs following the public disclosure of 33 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities — including full takeover exploits — that forced a worldwide shutdown of its hosted RMM platform. On-premises customers were urged to shut down immediately. N-central is used by MSPs to manage thousands of downstream customer environments, making any compromise a supply chain event affecting all managed endpoints.


An RMM platform returning from a forced global shutdown with a partial patch is still a high-risk supply chain event — MSPs and their downstream customers must verify hotfix deployment and assess exposure before restoring full operations.


Sources: BleepingComputer · Cybersecurity News


MCP Server Supply Chain Attack Surface: Post-Install Code Mutation Can Silently Steal API Keys and Admin Credentials


Nov 11, 16:07


Security researchers found that Model Context Protocol servers — the integration layer increasingly used to connect AI coding assistants to external tools — can modify their own code after installation, creating a supply chain attack vector. A single poisoned package in the MCP dependency chain could allow an attacker to silently exfiltrate API keys and administrator credentials used by AI agents. The finding is particularly acute because MCP servers often run with elevated permissions to serve AI coding tools.


MCP supply chain poisoning is a direct threat to any team running AI coding assistants with tool integrations — a new attack surface that security teams need to inventory and monitor now.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


eMudhra Revokes 8 More Intermediate CAs — 16 Total Pulled After Python Script Key Handling Failure


Nov 11, 12:00


Indian certificate authority eMudhra has revoked eight additional intermediate CAs, bringing the total to 16 revoked since October. The new eight had properly generated keys, but eMudhra could not demonstrate their private keys were handled according to its own procedures — a compliance failure that mandates revocation under CA/Browser Forum rules. Any certificates issued by the 16 affected intermediate CAs will be untrusted by browsers and operating systems.


Cascading CA revocations from a single scripting failure are expanding the blast radius — any organization with certificates issued by eMudhra's intermediate CAs needs to audit and reissue immediately.


Sources: The Hacker News · Cybersecurity News


AI & Machine Learning


Grok App Builder Exposes 35,000+ Apps — Business Data, Plain-Text Passwords, and Patient Records Accessible Without Login


Nov 11, 12:17


Security researchers found 35,578 of 37,571 apps built with xAI's Grok app builder are publicly accessible without authentication, including 24 apps built by X and SpaceXSI staff. Approximately one in ten of the exposed apps contains internal business data, staff information, plain-text passwords, or patient records. No exploitation was required — the apps were simply published publicly by default under grok.me.


Tens of thousands of AI-generated apps leaking credentials and patient data with no authentication required is a significant data exposure event — any organization whose staff has used Grok's builder needs to audit published apps immediately.


Sources: The Hacker News · Cybersecurity News


Google DeepMind Releases AlphaGenome 2 — Maps How DNA Changes Affect Individual Cell Types to Advance Disease Research


Nov 11, 15:00


Google DeepMind has unveiled AlphaGenome 2, a successor to its genome-predicting AI that models how the same DNA sequence produces different gene expression patterns across distinct cell types — from heart muscle to immune cells. The model gives researchers a more detailed view of how genetic variants contribute to disease at the cellular level, potentially pointing toward new treatment targets. The release follows DeepMind's recent formal verification of the Signal Protocol using AI agents, reinforcing its scientific AI momentum.


AlphaGenome 2's cell-type-specific gene expression modeling is a direct capability advance for anyone working in genomics, drug discovery, or precision medicine — and signals DeepMind's expanding lead in biological AI.


Sources: The Verge


Finland and Estonia Call for EU-Level AI Incident Response System Ahead of Friday Leaders' Summit


Nov 11, 16:19


In a letter seen by Politico, Finland and Estonia are calling on the EU to establish formal arrangements for responding to serious AI incidents at the bloc level — timed to coincide with European leaders meeting Friday to discuss AI for the first time. The two countries argue that the EU AI Act's provisions are insufficient for real-time incident response and coordination across member states. The push comes as AI-related harms and misuse incidents are accumulating faster than regulatory frameworks can absorb.


An EU-level AI incident response framework would directly shape how AI failures and misuse are classified, reported, and remediated across all 27 member states — a regulatory direction signal for any organization deploying AI in Europe.


Sources: Politico EU


Radical Numerics Builds AI Model to Detect AI-Engineered Bioweapons — Works Offline Without Internet Connection


Nov 11, 17:00


Startup Radical Numerics has developed an AI model it claims can identify both naturally occurring and AI-engineered pathogens without requiring an internet connection, targeting a biosecurity gap created by the growing accessibility of AI tools for pathogen design. The offline capability is designed to enable deployment in field environments and classified settings where connectivity is restricted. The startup positions itself as an AI-versus-AI countermeasure for one of the most concerning AI misuse vectors.


An AI specifically built to counter AI-engineered bioweapons represents a new defensive category emerging directly in response to dual-use biological AI risk — a signal for anyone tracking biosecurity or AI safety threat models.


Sources: Wired


Anthropic IPO: Insider Conflicts Scrutinized as Biggest Investors Are Also Key Business Partners


Nov 11, 13:40


A New York Times DealBook analysis examines the clubby structure of Anthropic's upcoming IPO, noting that the largest investors in the listing — Amazon, Google, and others — are simultaneously Anthropic's most critical cloud and distribution partners. Databricks Deploys Internal 'Genie' AI Agent to Give CEO Unfiltered Company Truth — Scales to 12,000 Employees


Nov 11, 15:00


Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi is using the company's newly revised Genie AI agent to surface candid internal intelligence he can't get from direct reports at a 12,000-person organization — including things that go wrong that employees wouldn't report up the chain. The agent synthesizes internal data to give Ghodsi an unvarnished view of company operations. The deployment illustrates a practical enterprise use case for AI agents: providing senior leaders with signal that organizational hierarchy normally filters out.


An AI agent built to bypass organizational reporting filters for executive decision-making is a concrete agentic deployment pattern directly relevant to anyone evaluating enterprise AI use cases at scale.

OpenAI Quarterly Revenue Crosses $10B for First Time — 50% Jump from Q2's $6.7B


Nov 11, 16:14


OpenAI's quarterly revenue has surpassed $10 billion for the first time, representing nearly a 50% increase from the $6.7 billion recorded in Q2 2026, according to reporting cited by TechCrunch. The milestone confirms ChatGPT's commercial scale but comes alongside continued steep operating losses as compute and infrastructure costs outpace revenue growth. The figure sets the benchmark for frontier AI commercial performance entering 2027.


OpenAI crossing $10B quarterly revenue resets the financial benchmark for the entire frontier AI sector — directly relevant to competitive positioning, pricing dynamics, and vendor sustainability assessments.

China's Nvidia Honeypot: How a Suspected Chinese Spy Gained Access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia Chips

The loss of Apple's community support archive affects millions of users and IT administrators who rely on community-sourced solutions — and signals Apple's shift toward AI-first support models.

November Patch Tuesday Update Failing to Install — KB5132061 Throws Errors, Microsoft Silent

Microsoft patched 1,259 vulnerabilities in its November 2026 Patch Tuesday — the second consecutive month exceeding 1,000 flaws — spanning Windows, Office, SharePoint, SQL Server, and developer tools. An exploited Outlook flaw leaking NTLMv2 hashes affects every organization running on-premises Exchange or Outlook — patch now.

Nov 11, 06:04


CISA added two actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog: CVE-2026-20320 in Cisco BroadWorks (CVSS 7.5, XML external entity injection) and CVE-2026-111793 in Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder, both allowing attackers to leak sensitive information including configuration data. Active exploitation of a carrier-grade UC platform confirms real-world attacker interest — any org running Cisco BroadWorks needs to assess exposure now.

AI Agent Backdoor With Fewer Than 10 Neuron Edits — Microsoft's 'Lazarus' Technique Requires No Retraining


Nov 11, 07:21


Microsoft researchers demonstrated a technique called Lazarus that plants a hidden backdoor in an AI model by editing fewer than 10 rarely-used neurons — no retraining required. When a chosen trigger appears in input, the backdoored model outputs attacker-controlled commands that an AI agent executes with its own permissions, enabling code download and execution. The attacker needs write access to model weights, making supply chain compromise, model distribution platforms, and fine-tuning pipelines the primary threat vectors.


A minimal-footprint, no-retraining backdoor technique for AI agents is a direct threat model for any organization deploying third-party or fine-tuned models in agentic workflows.

Railway has pledged to cover charges that AI providers will not refund. The incident illustrates a rapidly growing threat: secrets stored in PaaS environments being monetized directly through LLM API abuse rather than conventional data theft.


AI API key theft for LLMjacking is a maturing attack class — any team storing LLM provider keys in cloud platforms needs to audit secrets management and rotation practices.

Microsoft is retiring the free Office 365 A1 and Student Use Benefit tiers that have provided email and productivity tools to educational institutions at no cost, requiring schools to budget for paid replacements at their next renewal. The timing follows Microsoft's separate push to monetize AI features in education products.

An active ransomware attack on a major public library system is a public services disruption event and a continuing signal about the vulnerability of municipal and cultural institutions.

Royal Navy Deploys First Operational Autonomous Boat Squadron

The Royal Navy has stood up its first operational squadron of autonomous surface vessels, moving uncrewed maritime systems from experimental to operational status as part of its Hybrid Navy vision. The first operational autonomous boat squadron in a NATO navy is a milestone in military autonomy adoption — a signal for anyone tracking defense technology, autonomous systems, or maritime security.

US Military Aircraft Pulled From Second UK Base After Iran Threat — RAF Fairford Withdrawal Confirmed

China's trade surplus has exceeded $1 trillion in 2026 at a record pace, driven by surging factory exports finding buyers worldwide. The European Commission has initiated legal action against IBM and Atos over a €212 million border IT project that has missed deadlines repeatedly, seen costs balloon, and devolved into a blame game between the two vendors. The case is a cautionary tale for large-scale government IT procurement and reflects broader questions about Atos's financial and delivery stability.

DOJ Sues Lyft for Disability Discrimination — Drivers Routinely Denying Rides to Wheelchair Users and Service Animals

The Justice Department filed a lawsuit against Lyft alleging that the company and its drivers routinely deny rides to passengers with stowable wheelchairs or service animals, in violation of the Americans with Disabilities Act. The suit follows a broader DOJ pattern of enforcement actions against platform economy companies for ADA compliance failures and could force structural changes to how Lyft handles driver refusals.

France's foreign ministry formally attributed the October wave of cyberattacks on industrial refrigeration systems — which disrupted more than 700 supermarkets and retail locations across France and wider Europe, caused significant food losses, and sparked at least 15 fires — to Iran's IRGC Shahid Kaveh cyber unit, the same group previously linked to attacks on US water utility industrial controllers. The attribution connects directly to the US agencies' refrigeration controller advisory from earlier this window.


Nation-state attribution for the largest OT/ICS sabotage campaign on European soil — causing physical fires and threatening food and medical supply chains — is a landmark industrial cybersecurity event.

N-able has taken all hosted N-central cloud environments offline and urged on-premises customers to shut down their servers immediately after a security researcher publicly published more than 30 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities in the platform, including proof-of-concept exploits capable of full system takeover. N-central is a widely deployed remote monitoring and management platform used by managed service providers to administer thousands of end-customer environments. A compromise of N-central gives attackers downstream access to all managed endpoints.


An RMM platform going fully offline due to publicly disclosed takeover-level zero-days is a critical MSP supply chain event — any organization whose IT is managed by an N-able MSP is downstream of this risk.

A vulnerability in SSH daemon implementations on Linux devices is under active exploitation, allowing attackers to gain unauthorized SSH access to affected systems. The flaw affects a broad class of internet-facing Linux devices. CISA and security vendors are tracking active exploitation in the wild; patch availability and affected package details are confirmed but specific vendor advisories vary.


An actively exploited SSH vulnerability affecting internet-facing Linux infrastructure is a patch-now situation for any organization running Linux servers exposed to the internet.

Qubole Supply Chain Attack: Hackers Exploit Trusted AWS Integration to Access Multiple Customer Accounts and Steal Secrets

Attackers compromised credentials for the AWS account that Qubole's data lake platform uses to access customer environments, then used those trusted credentials to breach multiple customer AWS accounts between October 14–26, stealing stored secrets and sensitive data. Wiz discovered and reported the attack. How the initial Qubole credentials were obtained has not been disclosed. The attack is a classic trusted-third-party pivot — Qubole's platform legitimately needed broad AWS access, making it a high-value target.


A cloud data platform's trusted AWS credentials being weaponized to pivot into multiple customer environments is a textbook supply chain attack on cloud infrastructure — directly relevant to any org using Qubole or similar data platforms with cross-account AWS access.


Sources: The Hacker News · The Register


Vanderbilt University Hit by BYOD Ransomware — Databases Encrypted, Student and Research Data Stolen


Nov 9, 23:52


Vanderbilt University is responding to a ransomware attack claimed by the BYOD gang, which alleges it encrypted university databases and stole sensitive student, employee, and research data. The attack is actively developing, with campus devices and systems reported as impacted. Vanderbilt is a major research university with significant federal research contracts and medical center operations.


A ransomware and data theft attack on a major research university with federal research ties — including potential exposure of student and research data — is a significant higher education sector incident.


Sources: BleepingComputer · The Record


Claude 'Office Party' Flaw Actively Exploited to Execute Malicious Code on Linux — Document Processing Vulnerability


Nov 9, 18:08


Attackers are exploiting a flaw in Claude's document-processing tool that allows creation of a temporary file accessible and executable by Claude's AI assistant on a user's Linux machine, enabling arbitrary code execution. The vulnerability — nicknamed 'Office Party' — is being actively used in the wild, not just demonstrated as a proof of concept. Anthropic has not yet issued a patch timeline in available reporting.


An actively exploited RCE vulnerability in Claude's document tooling is a direct risk for any developer or enterprise running Claude-integrated workflows on Linux systems.


Sources: Dark Reading


Ethersphere Supply Chain Attack: Bee-js and Swarm Desktop Compromised via Release Automation to Steal Wallet Keys


Nov 9, 17:36


Attackers used Ethersphere's own release automation pipeline to publish malicious versions of bee-js (13.3.0) and Swarm Desktop (0.56.2), two tools for the Swarm decentralized storage network. The malicious releases steal the wallet key stored by Swarm Desktop along with the password unlocking it, and install a persistent backdoor. The attack is a software supply chain compromise using the project's own trusted release infrastructure.


Weaponizing a project's own release automation to distribute wallet-stealing malware is a supply chain attack pattern that extends well beyond crypto — any project using automated release pipelines faces this threat model.


Sources: The Hacker News


AI & Machine Learning


Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 — Solves Open Physics Problems, Enters Cisco and IBM Products


Nov 9, 19:00


Anthropic released two new models: Claude Fable 5.2, optimized for software engineering and agent orchestration, and Claude Mythos 5.2, a frontier reasoning model that Anthropic claims solved two open theoretical physics problems during prerelease testing. Both show improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision over the 5.1 versions. Separately, Anthropic confirmed Mythos is being integrated into Cisco and IBM security products for bug-finding, with enterprise customers accessing capabilities without receiving the model directly — a new enterprise deployment pattern.


A direct vendor release with claimed scientific breakthrough performance is mandatory coverage — and the Cisco/IBM enterprise integration signals a new distribution model for frontier AI capabilities.


Sources: Anthropic · The Verge · TechCrunch · The Register


Google Gemini Routing Personal Drive Files and Emails to Human Annotators — 649 HN Points


Nov 9, 18:24


A GitHub repository drawing 649 Hacker News points and 137 comments alleges that Google Gemini, when processing personal files and emails from connected Google Drive and Gmail accounts, is routing that content to human annotators for review. If confirmed at scale, this would represent a significant privacy disclosure gap for enterprise and consumer users who have connected their Google accounts to Gemini. Google has not publicly responded to the specific claims.


Alleged human review of personal Drive and email content processed by an AI assistant is a material enterprise privacy and compliance concern — and the HN traction signals broad practitioner alarm.


Sources: GitHub (original report)


Meta Releases Muse Ember — Lightweight Agent Execution Model at $0.10/M Tokens


Nov 9, 18:00


Meta released Muse Ember, described as its smallest and most efficient model, designed specifically for agent execution tasks rather than frontier reasoning. At 10 cents per million input tokens, Ember is significantly cheaper than competing small models like Anthropic's Haiku and OpenAI's Luna, positioning it as a cost-efficient option for high-volume agentic workloads. The release drew 313 HN points and 135 comments.


A direct vendor model release from Meta at a price point designed to undercut competitors in the fast-growing agent execution market is a mandatory signal on where the cost curve is heading.


Sources: Meta AI Research · TechCrunch


Google DeepMind Formally Verifies Signal Protocol Using AI Tool — Stretch Goal: Verify 'All the Software of the World'


Nov 10, 05:01


Google DeepMind researchers used a new AI-powered formal verification tool to prove that the Signal Protocol — the encryption standard underlying Signal, WhatsApp, and iMessage — is cryptographically sound and behaves exactly as intended. The tool automated much of the proof work that previously required months of expert human effort. DeepMind researchers described the stretch goal as applying the same approach to formally verify critical software at a global scale.


AI-assisted formal verification of a widely deployed cryptographic protocol is a landmark capability demonstration — and a direct counterpoint to the same team's work showing AI can break weaker cryptography.


Sources: Wired


Anthropic IPO Plans Move Forward — Valuation Range Expected This Week


Nov 10, 01:27


Anthropic is reportedly proceeding with its IPO plans and is expected to set its valuation range this week, according to the Wall Street Journal. The timing comes as the company releases two major new models (Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2) and expands enterprise distribution through Cisco and IBM integrations. The IPO would be one of the largest AI company public offerings to date.


Anthropic setting an IPO valuation range this week is a defining moment for AI company valuations and public market appetite for frontier AI — a key signal for the entire sector.

Scott Wiener Wins Nancy Pelosi's Congressional Seat — California's AI Regulation Author Now Heads to Congress

California State Senator Scott Wiener, author of the state's major AI safety legislation (SB 1047 and successors), won the congressional race for former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi's San Francisco seat and is now positioned to shape federal AI policy from Capitol Hill. Wiener has indicated he plans to pursue federal AI regulation, bringing the most substantive state-level AI legislative record of any incoming member of Congress. The architect of the most significant state AI safety legislation in the US just won a congressional seat — federal AI regulatory momentum has a new and experienced champion.


Sources: MIT Technology Review


Apple Introduces $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs — AI Features With Cloud Limits Now Cost Extra


Nov 9, 19:09


Apple has introduced 'Intelligence Usage Packs' — $49.99 one-time purchases that extend access to Apple Intelligence features with usage limits, first surfacing in Logic Pro. Apple introducing paid consumption tiers for AI features is a signal about how the company plans to monetize AI — and sets a precedent for how premium AI capabilities get priced in consumer software.

Wyndham confirmed the issue was resolved but said it does not have the technical capability to determine whether unauthorized access occurred before remediation. Wyndham operates more than 9,000 hotels globally.


A hardcoded credential in a major hotel chain's customer app — with no ability to audit past unauthorized access — is a significant consumer data exposure with identity and payment implications.

The USPS data supersedes commonly used Census ZCTA approximations.


Official USPS ZIP boundary data eliminates a long-standing data quality problem for every developer or analyst building location-aware systems — an immediate practical upgrade for geospatial work.


Sources: USPS Postal Pro


Infineon Produces First 300mm Silicon Carbide Wafer — Power Semiconductor Manufacturing Milestone

Infineon Technologies announced the production of the world's first 300-millimeter silicon carbide (SiC) wafer, a significant manufacturing milestone for power semiconductors used in electric vehicles, industrial inverters, and power electronics. The larger wafer format dramatically reduces cost per chip by increasing die yield per wafer, following the same economics that drove CMOS cost reductions over decades. SiC is the dominant semiconductor material for high-efficiency EV power conversion.


300mm SiC wafers will drive down EV and industrial power electronics costs significantly — a supply chain and cost curve signal for anyone tracking EV adoption, clean energy infrastructure, or semiconductor manufacturing.

Cisco to Mandate All Future Products Connect to Cloud Control SaaS Platform — Global Rollout 2027

Organizations that prefer on-premises or federated management will face increasing pressure as new products ship with mandatory cloud dependencies.
